hooks.name: Enforce Semantic In-Place Edits
hooks.description: Before any full-file write, enforce program analysis and language-server-driven, targeted in-place replacements instead of rewriting whole files.

action.prompt:
STRICT EDITING POLICY — read before writing this file.

You are about to perform a full-file write (fs_write). This is only permitted for creating a NEW file. For modifying an EXISTING file, full-file rewrites are prohibited.

Required behavior:
1. Analyze the program before editing. Read the relevant file(s) and understand the symbols, scope, and references involved.
2. Prefer the workspace language server for structural changes:
   - Use semantic_rename for renaming any symbol (variable, function, class, parameter) so all references update consistently.
   - Use smart_relocate for moving/renaming files so imports and references update automatically.
3. For content changes to an existing file, use str_replace for targeted in-place replacements (or fs_append to add to the end). Match the minimal surrounding context needed to disambiguate — do not restate unchanged regions.
4. Reserve fs_write strictly for brand-new files, or for a case where a targeted edit is genuinely impossible; if you must use it on an existing file, state explicitly why a targeted edit could not be used.

If you were about to rewrite an existing file wholesale, stop and redo the change as one or more targeted str_replace / semantic_rename / smart_relocate operations instead.
